---
title: Source and Tool
---

## Source and tool roles

A **source** retrieves documents. A **tool** exposes an action to the model. Keeping
them separate allows the same Elasticsearch, web, or file source to support search,
visit, or a custom tool interface.

Built-in sources:

| Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Full-text search and fetch under a local directory; requires `rg` |
| `elasticsearch` | BM25, vector, or hybrid retrieval from an Elasticsearch index |
| `web` | Serper search and Jina page fetch |
| `custom` | A project-defined `DataSource` implementation |

Built-in tools include `search`, `visit`, `multi_source_search`,
`multi_source_visit`, and `mcp`.

## Connect tools to sources

Each source has a unique `name`. Source-backed tools refer to those names:

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: docs
      root_path: ./docs

  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      source: [docs]
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [docs]
```

The source name is internal configuration. The tool name, description, and input
schema are visible to the model.

## Elasticsearch retrieval

Use `vector_search_mode: bm25`, `vector`, or `hybrid`. Vector and hybrid modes require
an embedding model endpoint and a populated vector field.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: corpus
      hosts: http://127.0.0.1:9200
      index: documents
      search_fields: [title, text]
      document_id_field: url
      fetch_field: url
      vector_search_mode: hybrid
      vector_field: text_vector
      embedding_model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
      embedding_base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8004/v1
      embedding_api_key: EMPTY
      es_max_concurrency: 256
      embedding_max_concurrency: 256
```

Set `highlight: true` to build compact, search-engine-style snippets from matching
fragments. Tune `highlight_fragment_size`, `highlight_number_of_fragments`, and
`snippet_chars` to control the returned context.

## Customize the model-visible tool

Tool behavior and model-facing presentation are configured independently:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_web
      description: Search the indexed web corpus for evidence.
      source: [corpus]
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          query:
            type: string
            description: A focused search query.
        required: [query]
        additionalProperties: false
      raise_argument_validation_error: false
```

`argument_mapping` can rename model-visible arguments before execution. Keep schemas
small and unambiguous: the model should see only arguments it can use correctly.

## Summarize large tool results

Search and visit tools can pass their output through a separate summarizer model:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [corpus]
      summary_goal_key: goal
      summarizer:
        model: Qwen3-8B
        base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1
        api_key: EMPTY
        max_chars: 40000
        max_concurrency: 128
        default_kwargs:
          max_tokens: 1024
        retry_config:
          max_tries: 3
```

The summarizer reduces context growth but adds latency and another failure surface.
Use it when raw documents are substantially larger than the evidence needed.

## MCP tools

Use `type: mcp` to expose a tool hosted by an MCP server. Configure the server
transport and remote tool name in the `ToolConfig` fields used by `MCPTool`. MCP tools
share the same initialization, validation, retry, and shutdown lifecycle as native
tools.

For custom retrieval, subclass `DataSource` and use `type: custom` with a `target`.
For custom model actions, subclass `BaseTool` and register the implementation with
`register_tool()` before building the agent.
